speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you are presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any changes in your bowel or bladder habits, such as difficulty urinating or feeling full quickly after eating?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, and CA-125 tumor markers.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic Ultrasound, Chest X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: WBC 8,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL, Platelets 275,000 /μL; CMP: NORMAL READINGS; CA-125: Level Normal; Chest X-Ray: Right-sided pleural effusion; Pelvic Ultrasound: Large mass in the right ovary, significant ascites present.

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol regularly. Works as a high school teacher.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, night sweats, chest pain, or swelling in the legs. She has not noticed any changes in bowel or urinary habits. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.
